records.query: Need the patient's resting electrocardiogram and continuous cardiac monitoring (Holter) results, along with serial cardiac troponin measurements, to confirm or exclude arrhythmic or ischemic causes of exertional dyspnea and syncope.
records.text:
- ECG findings:  Image Title: Initial ECG  Image Description: Shows sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block (PR interval 360 ms), right bundle-branch block (RBBB) and left anterior fascicular block (LAFB). Wide QRS complex (120 ms), rSR in lead V1, and RS in lead V6 (deep and wide S waves ≥40 ms). Left axis deviation and qR in leads I and aVL, and rS in leads II, III, and aVF.
- 24-hour ECG monitoring:  Image Title: Continuous ambulatory ECG monitoring  Image Description: Shows sinus rhythm (average 60 beats/min), PR prolongation (360 ms) and third-degree AV block with minimum heart rate of 36 beats/min. Mobitz type I second-degree AV block with pause and junctional escape beat observed. No atrial/ventricular arrhythmia found.

records.query: Need serial cardiac troponin measurements and an echocardiography report (core tests to determine whether the high-grade AV block is due to myocardial ischemia and to evaluate any structural heart disease).
records.text: Echocardiogram findings:  - Normal left ventricular ejection fraction (74%)  - Normal wall motion  - Left atrial enlargement (volume index, 34.89 mL/m2)  - Uncertain diastolic function  - No significant valvular abnormality  - Pulmonary hypertension (mean pulmonary arterial pressure 32 mm Hg)

bindings.label: Patient in their 80s presented with dyspnea and syncope during exercise
Medical history included essential hypertension and Parkinson disease
Patient reported dyspnea on exertion and exercise intolerance for the past year, with difficulty walking more than 100m
Patient experienced syncope during a bicycle ride with loss of consciousness for a few minutes, followed by complete recovery
Physical examination showed vital signs normal except elevated blood pressure of 150/78 mm Hg; chest auscultation revealed normal breath and heart sounds without murmurs
ECG/Holter confirmed first-degree AV block, RBBB/LAFB, and third-degree AV block with pauses (minimum heart rate 36 bpm)
Echocardiography showed normal wall motion, no valvular disease, and mild pulmonary hypertension
Troponin and coronary angiography results are unavailable
Third-degree AV block with bifascicular block is the specific cardiac cause of the patient's exertional dyspnea and syncope
Laboratory tests were normal, not supporting electrolyte or thyroid abnormalities as reversible causes
ECG/Holter showed junctional escape rhythm during third-degree AV block
Echocardiography estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure at 32 mmHg (mild pulmonary hypertension)
Positron emission tomography showed increased uptake in the left adrenal gland with a standardized uptake value of 7.4
